title: Live sales call: discover, qualify, demonstrate, handle objections
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: How to run a sales call so it ends with qualification and a dated next step, and how to handle price gaps, trial requests and objections.
applies_when: Considered purchase with a call or meeting step
evidence_requirements: what the lead asked for and how they arrived
public facts about the account (site, listings, job posts)
offer facts: price ranges, proof items, case results
stated problem in the buyer's words
evidence the problem is material (volume, cost, deadline)
whether the buyer pays for any solution to this or similar problems
who decides and how purchases happen
the objection in the buyer's words
proof items and pricing rules in confirmed facts
value themes with the features behind each
proof inventory tagged by industry, role, starting status quo
common unspoken objections from lost/stalled deals
missing_data_behavior: No proof assets: say so; no invented logos or results.

decision_branches.then: Disqualify only if they never pay for solutions.

implementation_steps: Pre-call note (10-15 min): pain signals, size of the job, current solution, who decides, known unknowns, call goal.
Open: agree the agenda and that the call may end early if it is not a fit (micro-contract).
Discovery: problem, size, current workaround and its cost, consequence of doing nothing, who uses it, who decides, how they buy, timing.
Show only what maps to their stated problem, using their data or realistic sample data.
Proof: one or two results from confirmed facts.
Price framed against their current cost or alternative; then stop talking.
Direct ask, or a trial close if signals are unclear.
Agree and calendar the next step; same-day summary email.
Record each qualification field as unknown / reported / verified / contradicted (Book 11 §4 states).
Ask the cheapest missing question next.
Catch the objection and restate it.
Find the question under the question.
Answer with one concrete proof or the buyer's own numbers.
Up to three value themes, each: claim, features that deliver it, demo or slide
Proof per theme matched to the prospect
dependencies: A deal size that pays for a live conversation (BRP-19 motion fit)
Confirmed facts for price and proof; otherwise [NEEDS FACT]
A written ideal-customer description with disqualifiers (Book 11 §2)
A living objection list with approved answers and proof (owner-maintained)
confirmed facts for timelines, certifications, integrations

cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: owner time: ~15 min prep + call + ~15 min follow-up per meeting
cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: a short pitch narrative and 1-2 proof items
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: meetings held, qualified share, next-step agreed share, proposals requested

metrics: share ending with a calendared next step
share of held meetings later marked unqualified
share of trial requests resolved by proof without a pilot
share of first calls with an agreed next step
share of bad-fit prospects exiting at call one rather than later
guardrails: Written follow-ups get one objection attempt; live calls may take distinct objections in turn; a repeated no is final.
Parity requirements (e.g. SOC 2) go under objections, not value; never raise an objection you can't answer.
No invented prices, results or customers
Recording or transcription only with consent where law requires
Use only business-relevant public facts in research (no personal social-media profiling)
Job title does not prove authority; stage label does not prove probability (Book 11 prohibited inferences)
Never mark a field verified from a similar customer
One attempt per objection in written follow-ups
No invented discounts, deadlines or results
Pilot success criteria agreed in writing before start
Deployment times, certifications and customer names only from confirmed facts
Your own claim is not proof
alternatives_when_constrained: Low price or no time for calls: recorded demo video, published FAQ/objections page, self-serve trial (BRP-19)
No proof yet: offer a small paid first project instead of claiming results
Too few deals to compute shares: review each lost/unqualified deal by hand
No proof items yet: offer a small paid first step or money-back terms if the owner approves
Self-serve product: a time-boxed trial with onboarding emails instead of a guided session
No proof yet: demo the mechanism, offer a pilot as the ask, mark proof as [NEEDS FACT]
stop_conditions: Review the script after every ~10 held meetings: which questions predicted wins, which slides confused
If unqualified-after-meeting share is high for two review periods, fix targeting or booking questions before adding more outreach
Any objection heard 2+ times: add an approved answer and proof item to the living list
Very frequent objection: address it up front in the pitch or landing page
If next-step agreement stays low after the test period, check the ask's complexity before the story
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Feature tour without discovery ('show up and throw up')
Skipping the price and the ask out of fear of rejection
Strict BANT applied to a category buyers did not know existed
Treating a friendly contact as the decision-maker
Unstructured free trials for products that need setup (low use, blamed on product)
Same case study for every prospect

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: A sales-call plan must end with one agreed, dated next step or an explicit disqualification; 'I'll send info, let me know' is not a next step.
proposed: Recommend a separate discovery call only when the demo needs more than ~15 minutes; otherwise one meeting (each extra meeting adds no-show risk).
proposed: 'No budget line' alone never disqualifies; 'never pays for solutions to problems like this' does, unless the owner overrides.
proposed: For price objections, ask the size of the gap before answering; route small gaps to negotiation levers and large gaps to value math or scope change.
proposed: Never recommend an unstructured free trial for an offer that needs setup or training; recommend a guided session or a structured pilot with written success criteria.
proposed: every pitch output ends with exactly one primary next step

external_requirement.rule: proposed: Call plans never include recording or transcription unless the owner confirms consent handling for the jurisdiction.
proposed: certifications and deployment-time statements in pitches pass the existing claim lint

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: Do not draft live-call scripts when the price per customer cannot pay for a human sale; route to BRP-19 alternatives.
proposed: Do not recommend discounting to win a buyer whose expected value from the offer is low; recommend disqualifying.
proposed: Structured pilots only when expected deal value covers the owner hours of the pilot (computed by code from owner inputs).

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: Track 'unqualified after a meeting' separately from 'lost'; a rising share points to targeting or booking questions (diagnostic hypothesis, not proven cause).
proposed: In written follow-ups, one evidenced answer per objection; a repeated no ends the sequence.
proposed: a value theme that every shortlisted alternative also delivers is moved to objections or parity notes

reconciliation_note: No skill covered the live call before.
